title: Two-Way Frequency Tables & Conditional Probability
sub: 20 SPRs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Official Digital SAT Curriculum

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A survey asked adults in two neighborhoods whether they support building a new park. The results are shown in the table. If one adult is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the adult is in the category Southside and Support?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $5/48$. There are 10 such adults out of 96 total, so the probability is $\frac{10}{96} = \frac{5}{48}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A group of students was asked whether they prefer to study in the morning or in the evening. The results are shown in the table, by grade level. If one student is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the student is in the category Grade 11 and Morning?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $9/106$. There are 9 such students out of 106 total, so the probability is $\frac{9}{106} = \frac{9}{106}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A bookstore recorded the format of the books it sold in one week, by genre. The results are shown in the table. If one book is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the book is in the category Fiction and Digital?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $11/26$. There are 55 such books out of 130 total, so the probability is $\frac{55}{130} = \frac{11}{26}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A city surveyed commuters about how they travel to work, by age group. The results are shown in the table. If one commuter is selected at random from the group, what is the probability that the commuter is in the category Under 30 and Car?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $15/64$. There are 30 such commuters out of 128 total, so the probability is $\frac{30}{128} = \frac{15}{64}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A survey of $178$ employees found that $12$ are in the Marketing department and working remotely, $118$ are in the Marketing department and working on-site, $35$ are not in the Marketing department and working remotely, and $13$ are not in the Marketing department and working on-site. What is the probability that a randomly selected employee is in the Marketing department?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $65/89$. $P(\text{in the Marketing department})=\frac{130}{178}=65/89$

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A bag contains $5$ red marbles and $15$ blue marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is red?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $1/4$. Applying Probability, Conditional Probability & Two-Way Tables principles, $P(\text{red})=\frac{5}{20}=1/4$ Therefore, the verified correct option is 1/4.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A survey of $178$ shoppers found that $47$ are using a coupon and spending over USD 50, $75$ are using a coupon and spending USD 50 or less, $25$ are not using a coupon and spending over USD 50, and $31$ are not using a coupon and spending USD 50 or less. What is the probability that a randomly selected shopper is using a coupon?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $61/89$. $P(\text{using a coupon})=\frac{122}{178}=61/89$

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: A survey of $207$ voters found that $81$ are under 40 years old and supporting the proposal, $5$ are under 40 years old and opposing the proposal, $57$ are 40 years old or older and supporting the proposal, and $64$ are 40 years old or older and opposing the proposal. questions.answer: **Answer:** $81/86$. $P(\text{supporting the proposal}\mid\text{under 40 years old})=\frac{81}{86}=81/86$
